messages.subject: Build a (numerically stable) linear equation - based probability
parts:
Hello,

I am running the code with my defined density function (y = a * x + c). The function is defined inclusive between x=[1, 2] with y > 0 within this interval.

c and a can both be ><= 0


The problem is that:
Enter code here...

1) if I use the logaritmic transformation of such formula (from: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_logarithmic_identities)

with x ~ uniform(1,2); //prior stage

functions {
 real linear_fx_log(real phi, real x, real a, real c) {
   return log(c) + log1p((a*x)/c);
 }
}
phi ~ linear_fx(x, a, c);



I get this error

log(0) = -Inf. Probably because c can be = 0


2) if I calculate the logarithm outside the formula

with x ~ uniform(1,2); //prior stage

functions {
 real linear_fx_log(real phi, real x, real a, real c) {
   return c + (a * x);
 }
}

phi ~ linear_fx(x, a, c);
log(phi)


The simulation runs but gives these errors:

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Build a (numerically stable) linear equation - based probability
parts:
You need to constrain the density so that it has support
on the declared constraints on parameters. So if a and c aren't
constrained on sign, but y needs to be > 0, then you have to set
up constraints to guarantee

1 * a + c > 0
2 * a + c > 0

so that

real a;
real<lower=fmax(-a, -2 * a)> c;

I think that'll make sure the constraint's satisifed, but you should
check my algebra.

- Bob

parts:
Sorry Bob,

I realized I didn't explain the whole picture. c and a are within the data, they are not parameters.

Below you find the model. This LDA model imply that the probability of a word happening in a topic is expressed as linear function where the explanatory variable is (let's say) the humor of a person (this is a parallelism for a bio-informatic problem).

functions {
  real linear_fx_log(real phi, real x, real a, real c) {

//if(a > 0) return log(c) + log1p((a*x)/c);
    //else return log(c) + log1m((-a*x)/c);
    return (a*x) + c; // THIS LINE //
  }
} 
data {
  int<lower=2> K;               // num topics
  int<lower=2> W;               // num words
  int<lower=1> M;               // num docs
  int<lower=1> N;               // total word instances
  int<lower=0> tot_w_count;     //upper value for word counts
  vector<lower=0, upper=tot_w_count>[N] w_count;   // word count per document (e.g., cat in document 1 is present 5 times)
  int<lower=1,upper=W> w[N];    // word n
  int<lower=1,upper=M> doc[N];  // doc ID for word n
  vector<lower=0>[K] alpha;     // topic prior

  matrix[K, W] c;  // THIS LINE //
  matrix[K, W] a;  // THIS LINE //
}
parameters {
  simplex[K] theta[M];   // topic dist for doc m   
  real phi; //matrix[K,W] phi; // word dist for topic k    
  vector<lower=1.0,upper=2.0>[M] x;  // THIS LINE //
} 
model {
  for (m in 1:M) {
    theta[m] ~ dirichlet(alpha);  // prior 
    x[m] ~ uniform(1,2); //prior stage  // THIS LINE //
  }
  for (n in 1:N) {       
    real gamma[K];    
    for (k in 1:K) {
      phi ~ linear_fx(x[doc[n]], a[k,w[n]], c[k,w[n]]);  // THIS LINE //
      gamma[k] <- (log(theta[doc[n],k]) + log(phi));
    }
    if(w_count[n]>0) increment_log_prob(log_sum_exp(gamma) * w_count[n]);  // likelihood
  }
}

c and a are provided with the data and I know that x[1,2] * a + c > 0 for any c and a that I provide.

So, your suggested constrain
